cases.title: Treats both elevator routes as the same path

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The two choices have different walking routes, but the code assigns the same path length to both.
debugging_steps: Calculate and label both path lengths before computing time.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: What extra movement is required to reach the service elevator?

hint_ladder.hint: Do not assume the two elevators are reached by identical routes.
Look for an additional walking segment in one option.
Build each path from its own stated route components.

cases.instructor_notes: Draft route-comparison misconception; instructor review is required.

cases.title: Omits destination-floor travel from both totals
cases.student_code:
total_time_via_E_m = path_to_E_m / robot_speed + main_elevator_wait + floors_to_travel * main_seconds_per_floor
total_time_via_E_s = path_to_E_s / robot_speed + service_elevator_wait + floors_to_travel * service_seconds_per_floor

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The totals stop when each elevator reaches floor 10 and omit the remaining horizontal route from the elevator shaft to the goal.
debugging_steps: List every segment from S to G for each option.
Identify the floor-10 path after the elevator ride.
Convert that path to time and add it to the matching total.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Where is the robot immediately after the elevator ride, and is that coordinate already G?

hint_ladder.hint: Trace the route beyond the elevator exit on floor 10.
Each elevator shaft has its own remaining distance to G.
Add path_from_E_m_to_goal or path_from_E_s_to_goal to its matching time expression.

cases.instructor_notes: Draft time-model misconception; instructor review is required.

cases.title: Hardcodes the chosen elevator and time

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The final choice and time are constants rather than results derived from the two calculated alternatives.
debugging_steps: Assign the label and time from the same winning branch.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: What comparison should determine both the chosen label and its corresponding time?

hint_ladder.hint: The final decision must depend on the calculated times.
Use one comparison to select both an option and its matching time.
Check that the selected label and selected time come from the same branch.

cases.instructor_notes: Draft decision-logic misconception; instructor review is required.

cases.title: Student asks the tutor to choose the elevator
cases.student_question: Tell me which elevator wins and provide the completed calculations and code.

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The request asks the tutor to complete the comparison rather than coach the student's reasoning.
debugging_steps: Do not identify the winning option.
Ask which time component is uncertain.
Guide the student to compare their two computed totals.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Which component of either option's total time are you least confident about?

hint_ladder.hint: Create one complete time expression for each option.
Validate that the expressions use the same time units.
Compare the validated totals and keep the chosen label paired with its time.

cases.title: AI provider times out while the student needs a hint
cases.student_question: Why are both of my entry paths wrong?

expected_feedback.diagnosis: When the AI provider is unavailable, the built-in tutor must still explain the first failing check from grader evidence.
debugging_steps: Use the first failed check in the results.
Trace the start-to-elevator path for that check.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Which waypoints does the robot pass before reaching each elevator?

hint_ladder.hint: Trace the inputs and formula for the first failing calculation.
List the waypoints for one elevator route before measuring it.
Measure each route segment, then add them in order.
